title: Boundary Score Matching for Functional-Geometry Counterfactuals
title_zh: 面向功能几何反事实的边界得分匹配
hook: On minimal geometry flips, whole-chunk feasibility tuning can reduce invalid rollouts while lowering alternative-positive coverage; boundary-local shaping should improve edited-scene success without that coverage loss. The surprising result is the sign split between physical reliability and per-mode retention, not another average-success gain.
abstract_draft: Continuous-action vision-language-action policies can execute an action successfully in one scene yet fail after a small geometry edit that leaves the task and most of the trajectory unchanged. Recent work adds explicit feasibility supervision [semanticscholar:dd324415c99589f1f7f9b63eaa3a64a7ae042df2], geometry-guided action manifolds [semanticscholar:8cb14cd9dafae88163a7685336a02ac6c41ed646], or geometry-aware representations [dblp:journals/corr/abs-2606-08530], but their aggregate objectives do not identify where feasibility first flips or whether suppressing the invalid action erases other valid modes. We propose Boundary-Local Score Matching (BLSM): compile same-action minimal geometry flips, certify the first contiguous violation segment, apply a reference-adjusted feasible-versus-invalid score preference only on that segment, anchor scores on its complement, and preserve every compiler-enumerated feasible alternative independently. The proposal is falsified if violation-mask or pair-identity permutations retain the edited-scene and mode-coverage gains, or if removing alternative-positive preservation leaves worst-mode success unchanged when coverage is already high. Conditional on non-negligible pair eligibility and mode-roster support, BLSM should increase edited-scene success and reduce invalid execution without the alternative-positive coverage loss induced by global or whole-chunk feasibility shaping. The intended contribution is therefore a mechanism-level sign split between physical reliability and per-mode retention, rather than another average-success improvement.

motivation.problem_framing:
Functional geometry changes define a structural problem class in which the instruction, manipulated objects, and much of a candidate action remain stable while a small change in clearance, pose, or contact geometry changes the feasible action set. A continuous-action VLA trained by ordinary imitation receives no direct signal about that decision boundary. Global feasibility supervision can reject an invalid rollout, but it spreads credit over an entire action chunk and can depress nearby actions that remain physically valid. The core bottleneck is therefore not merely recognizing geometry; it is assigning a feasibility change to the first trajectory segment that actually violates the edited scene while retaining the other valid modes.

The closest adjacent systems address pieces of this structure but leave the credit-and-retention question unresolved. Explicit feasibility supervision targets invalid actions [semanticscholar:dd324415c99589f1f7f9b63eaa3a64a7ae042df2], Action Manifold Learning constrains prediction to geometry-guided valid regions [semanticscholar:8cb14cd9dafae88163a7685336a02ac6c41ed646], KeyStone selects a dominant consistent action cluster [semanticscholar:4a71dc5d2b6b4ea2a6477ec4515d8294e3c75383], GEAR-VLA aligns geometry-aware representations [dblp:journals/corr/abs-2606-08530], and STARRY couples future spatial-temporal latents to actions [semanticscholar:f134eaaeb2cf6d4ac3526993199033b7f858a35b]. None of the available records establishes a matched minimal edit, first-violation credit mask, complement-drift constraint, and mode-wise retention target in one mechanism. BLSM turns that residue into an identifiable training object: the score change that should occur at a certified feasibility boundary, separated from the score changes that should not occur elsewhere.
motivation.why_now: The gap is timely because recent VLA work has made geometry and continuous-action structure explicit enough to support controlled boundary construction: Pointing-VLA exposes typed spatial grounding [semanticscholar:aaef4e8a3bd4a3a4f6673b2d4bce0a3237783cb9], WNM-3D maintains persistent 3D context [semanticscholar:74257100ad8c273b90dbaaba190e1f699ec9df0a], Action Manifold Learning supplies a geometry-guided validity view [semanticscholar:8cb14cd9dafae88163a7685336a02ac6c41ed646], and KeyStone makes action-mode structure measurable [semanticscholar:4a71dc5d2b6b4ea2a6477ec4515d8294e3c75383]. Together with scripted RoboTwin 2.0 scene edits and a frozen continuous-action reference policy, these ingredients permit paired counterfactuals, simulator-certified violation masks, and per-mode score accounting that earlier aggregate feasibility objectives could not expose.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: Can Explicit Physical Feasibility Benefit VLA Learning? studies a geometry-grounded feasibility objective for suppressing physically invalid robot actions.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: Its available abstract does not establish same-action minimum geometry flips, first-violation-local score credit, complement anchoring, or independent retention of every feasible alternative mode.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: The missing ingredient is a paired boundary-construction and temporal-localization instrument; full-text absence also prevents verifying whether any equivalent mechanism is present.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: Learning Action Manifold with Multi-view Latent Priors predicts actions on a geometry-guided valid manifold to reduce monocular ambiguity and inefficient regression.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It does not use a minimal geometry intervention to measure which formerly valid mode becomes invalid or explicitly preserve worst-case retention across the remaining valid modes.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Its representation-level manifold objective lacks the paired score-change estimand and mode-indexed preservation mechanism required for boundary-local credit.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: Geometry Guided Self-Consistency for Physical AI samples candidate actions and executes the medoid of the largest geometry-consistent cluster.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It does not treat minority feasible clusters as protected positives or test whether feasibility shaping preserves each alternative mode after a geometry flip.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Largest-cluster aggregation removes mode identity from the objective, so it has no measurement or loss term for compiler-relative worst-mode retention.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: GEAR-VLA aligns 3D features and learns a canonicalized continuous-action expert for more generalizable manipulation.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It does not construct identical-action feasibility flips, localize the first violating segment, or separate necessary local score change from unwanted complement drift.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Its primary object is geometry-aware representation transfer rather than an interventional temporal credit signal with matched retention diagnostics.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: STARRY jointly denoises future spatial-temporal latents and actions through depth-conditioned attention for manipulation.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It does not estimate a reference-adjusted margin from a controlled validity flip or constrain action-score drift outside the simulator-certified violation segment.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Joint future-and-action denoising supplies no matched counterfactual boundary label or unique decomposition-derived supervisory signal.

motivation.what_changes_when_gap_closes: Closing this gap would let a VLA learn that a particular contact or clearance segment must change after a geometry edit while retaining all other feasible ways to finish the task. It would also make the reliability-diversity trade-off measurable: feasibility methods such as [semanticscholar:dd324415c99589f1f7f9b63eaa3a64a7ae042df2] and geometry-guided action methods such as [semanticscholar:8cb14cd9dafae88163a7685336a02ac6c41ed646] could be judged not only by invalid-action suppression, but by complement drift, alternative-positive coverage, and worst-mode success.

core_claim: On same-action minimal geometry flips, first-violation-local reference-adjusted score shaping with complement and alternative-mode anchoring can suppress invalid execution without the feasible-mode coverage loss caused by global or whole-chunk shaping.

sub_claims.statement: A minimum feasibility-flipping scene edit holding task and action identity fixed isolates a functional-geometry boundary rather than a generic scene-distribution shift.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Identifiability of the geometry-induced feasibility bottleneck

sub_claims.statement: A simulator-certified first-violation mask assigns the feasible-versus-invalid score preference only where the edited geometry first changes execution validity, while complement anchoring limits unrelated score drift.
Mode-wise anchoring of every compiler-enumerated feasible alternative prevents the local negative signal from collapsing minority valid modes.
Pair-eligibility gates and mask, identity, and preservation interventions distinguish the proposed boundary mechanism from generic extra supervision or selected-subset effects.

key_equations.latex: \Delta g^*=\arg\min_{\Delta g} C(\Delta g)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad F(x,a^-)=1,\;F(x\oplus\Delta g,a^-)=0
key_equations.description: The compiler chooses the lowest-cost geometry edit that flips the identical action chunk from feasible to infeasible.
key_equations.description_zh: 编译器寻找代价最小的几何改动，使同一动作片段从可行变为不可行。

key_equations.description: The mask is the first contiguous simulator-certified violation run beginning at the earliest violating time τ.
key_equations.description_zh: 掩码取从最早违规时刻 τ 开始、由模拟器确认的首个连续违规区间。

key_equations.description: Every action score is expressed as a change from the frozen reference policy, preventing raw score scale from defining the preference.
key_equations.description_zh: 动作得分以相对冻结参考策略的变化量表示，避免原始得分尺度主导偏好。

key_equations.latex: d_\theta^{(k)}=\frac{\sum_t m_t[\Delta_\theta(a^+_{k,t}\mid x')-\Delta_\theta(a^-_t\mid x')]}{\sum_t m_t},\quad \mathcal{L}_B=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\log(1+e^{-d_\theta^{(k)}}),\quad M_B=\mathbb{E}[d_\theta]
key_equations.description: The boundary loss increases the masked reference-adjusted margin of each feasible alternative over the invalid action; M_B is the held-out mean margin.
key_equations.description_zh: 边界损失提升每个可行替代动作相对无效动作的掩码参考校正间隔；M_B 是留出数据上的平均间隔。

key_equations.description: Complement anchoring limits off-boundary drift, while the equally weighted alternative loss anchors every feasible mode rather than only the dominant one.
key_equations.description_zh: 补集锚定限制边界外漂移；等权替代项逐一保护所有可行模式，而非只保护主导模式。

key_equations.description: BLSM adds boundary preference, complement stability, and mode preservation to the ordinary imitation objective; the three weights are selected once on validation pairs and then frozen.
key_equations.description_zh: BLSM 在常规模仿目标上加入边界偏好、补集稳定与模式保护；三个权重在验证对上一次选定后固定。

method_flow.high_level_pipeline: BLSM starts from successful RoboTwin action chunks and compiles the smallest scene-geometry edits that make the identical chunk invalid while preserving the task. Simulator replay identifies the first contiguous violation segment and enumerates the feasible alternative-action roster in the edited scene. A frozen reference policy converts candidate scores into score changes; training then prefers each feasible alternative over the invalid chunk only inside the violation mask, anchors the mask complement, and separately anchors every feasible mode. The resulting post-trained policy is characterized by its held-out boundary margin, edited-scene validity, complement drift, alternative-positive coverage, and worst-mode retention.

steps.title: Compile minimal feasibility flips
steps.what_changes: For each frozen-policy action chunk that succeeds in an original RoboTwin 2.0 scene, search the scene compiler over task-preserving geometry edits and retain the minimum-cost edit that makes the identical chunk fail; record every attempted pair and its inclusion or exclusion reason.
steps.why_this_step: Holding task and action identity fixed makes geometry-induced feasibility the only intended difference and exposes whether eligible boundary pairs occupy more than a selected corner of the data.
steps.input: Original RoboTwin 2.0 scenes, task instructions, frozen-policy action chunks, and simulator feasibility checks
steps.output: Accepted original/edited BoundaryFlip pairs plus a complete eligibility ledger

steps.title: Certify the first violation run
steps.what_changes: Replay the identical chunk in both scenes, compute the simulator violation indicator at each action time, and set m to the first contiguous violating run in the edited scene rather than labeling the full chunk.
steps.why_this_step: The decomposition is derived from observed simulator structure and yields the unique temporal region on which the geometry edit first changes functional validity.
steps.input: An accepted BoundaryFlip pair and synchronized simulator traces
steps.output: A nonempty first-violation mask m and its complement

steps.title: Enumerate feasible alternative modes
steps.what_changes: Run the same task compiler in the edited scene to enumerate feasible action chunks, partition them by the compiler's action-mode identity, and retain one scored roster entry for every supported mode rather than only the largest cluster.
steps.why_this_step: A mode-indexed roster makes positive coverage and worst-mode retention observable and prevents dominant-mode aggregation from hiding feasible alternatives.
steps.input: Edited scene, task specification, and compiler-generated feasible solutions
steps.output: Alternative-positive roster A+ with mode identities and roster-size metadata

steps.title: Match boundary-local score changes
steps.what_changes: Evaluate the trainable and frozen-reference action scores for the invalid chunk and each feasible alternative under the edited observation, form their reference-adjusted difference, and apply a feasible-over-invalid soft preference only at times selected by m.
steps.why_this_step: Reference adjustment isolates post-training movement, while mask-local preference directs feasibility credit to the segment implicated by the counterfactual rather than the whole action chunk.
steps.input: Violation mask, invalid action chunk, alternative-positive roster, edited observation, and frozen reference policy
steps.output: Boundary preference loss L_B and per-mode margins d_theta

steps.title: Anchor the complement and every positive
steps.what_changes: Penalize reference-adjusted score drift outside m for all rostered chunks and add an equal-per-mode score anchor for every feasible alternative, without pooling alternatives by frequency.
steps.why_this_step: The complement term prevents temporal credit leakage, and the alternative term makes suppression of minority feasible modes costly even when average validity improves.
steps.input: Reference-adjusted scores, mask complement, and the full alternative-positive roster
steps.output: Complement loss L_comp and alternative-preservation loss L_alt

steps.title: Optimize and expose the boundary diagnostics
steps.what_changes: Add L_B, L_comp, and L_alt to ordinary imitation, select their symbolic weights on validation pairs by first preventing complement and worst-mode degradation and then improving boundary separation, freeze the selected weights, and report M_B together with eligibility, mask-length, roster-size, drift, coverage, and worst-mode summaries.
steps.why_this_step: A constrained selection rule prevents an arbitrary loss-weight trade-off from masquerading as the mechanism, while the exposed diagnostics connect score movement to downstream reliability and retention.
steps.input: Imitation batches and the three BLSM loss terms
steps.output: A post-trained continuous-action VLA and boundary-mechanism diagnostics

method_flow.design_reasoning_echo: The design assumes that the simulator's feasibility predicate is correct for the task, the compiler's accepted edit is sufficiently minimal to isolate functional geometry, the first contiguous violation run captures the earliest operative failure, and the enumerated roster represents the feasible alternatives; each premise is exposed through eligibility, mask-length, roster-size, and exclusion reports rather than hidden in preprocessing. The observation model is conditional on compiler-attempted simulator pairs, so the estimand is the held-out reference-adjusted feasible-versus-invalid score margin at an accepted geometry boundary, not an unrestricted real-world causal effect. A naive global feasibility loss can suppress the invalid chunk but cannot say where the score should change and can lower nearby valid modes. BLSM therefore couples the decomposition-derived boundary preference with the two invariances implied by that decomposition: little score movement off the boundary and no mode-wise loss on feasible alternatives. Mask and identity permutations, plus removal of the alternative anchor, directly test whether these components—not generic extra supervision—produce the downstream sign split.

plain_motivation_en:
A small change in clearance, pose, or contact geometry can change which actions are feasible even when the instruction, objects, and much of an action stay the same. Ordinary imitation gives a continuous-action vision-language-action (VLA) policy no direct signal for this boundary. Global feasibility supervision can reject an invalid rollout, but may spread the correction across the whole action chunk and lower the scores of nearby actions that remain physically valid. The key need is to assign the change to the first segment that actually violates the edited scene while retaining other valid modes.

Related systems provide geometry-aware validity, action manifolds, action-cluster selection, geometry-aware representations, or spatial-temporal action conditioning, but the available records do not combine a matched minimal edit, first-violation credit, complement anchoring, and mode-wise retention. Boundary-Local Score Matching (BLSM) makes the needed score change at a certified feasibility boundary distinct from score changes that should not occur elsewhere.

Recent VLA work and scripted RoboTwin 2.0 edits provide typed spatial grounding, persistent 3D context, geometry-guided validity, measurable action modes, paired counterfactuals, simulator-certified masks, and per-mode score accounting. A frozen continuous-action reference policy supplies the comparison needed for these score changes.

Closing the gap lets a VLA change the score for a particular contact or clearance segment after a geometry edit while retaining other feasible ways to finish the task. Reliability and diversity can then be measured together through invalid-action suppression, complement drift, alternative-positive coverage, and worst-mode success.
plain_motivation_zh:
当间隙、姿态或接触几何发生很小变化时，可行动作集合可能改变，而指令、物体和动作的大部分仍保持不变。普通模仿学习不会直接告诉连续动作视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略这个边界在哪里。全局可行性监督可以拒绝无效轨迹，但可能把修正分摊到整个动作片段，并降低附近仍然物理可行的动作得分。因此，需要把变化归因到编辑场景中最先发生违规的片段，同时保留其他有效模式。

相关系统分别提供几何感知的有效性、动作流形、动作簇选择、几何感知表示或时空动作条件，但现有记录没有把匹配的最小编辑、首次违规得分归因、边界外锚定和逐模式保留结合起来。Boundary-Local Score Matching (BLSM) 将认证可行性边界处应发生的得分变化，与其他位置不应发生的变化区分开。

近期 VLA 工作和脚本化 RoboTwin 2.0 场景编辑提供了类型化空间定位、持久 3D 上下文、几何引导有效性、可测量的动作模式、成对反事实、模拟器认证的掩码和逐模式得分统计。冻结的连续动作参考策略提供了比较这些得分变化所需的基准。

弥合这一缺口后，VLA 可以在几何编辑后改变特定接触或间隙片段的得分，同时保留其他完成任务的可行方式。这样可以同时通过无效动作抑制、边界外漂移、替代正例覆盖率和最差模式成功率衡量可靠性与多样性。

plain_method_steps_en.what_to_do: For each frozen-policy action chunk that succeeds in an original RoboTwin 2.0 scene, search task-preserving geometry edits and keep the minimum-cost edit that makes the identical chunk fail. Record every attempted pair and why it is included or excluded. The input is the original scenes, task instructions, frozen-policy chunks, and simulator feasibility checks; the output is accepted original/edited BoundaryFlip pairs and a complete eligibility ledger.
plain_method_steps_en.why_this_makes_sense: Keeping the task and action identity fixed makes the geometry change the intended difference and shows whether eligible boundary pairs are broader than a selected corner of the data.

plain_method_steps_en.what_to_do: Replay the identical chunk in both scenes, compute the simulator violation indicator at each action time, and set m to the first contiguous violating run in the edited scene instead of labeling the full chunk. The input is an accepted BoundaryFlip pair and synchronized simulator traces; the output is a nonempty first-violation mask m and its complement.
plain_method_steps_en.why_this_makes_sense: The mask follows observed simulator structure and identifies the temporal region where the geometry edit first changes functional validity.

plain_method_steps_en.what_to_do: Run the task compiler in the edited scene to enumerate feasible action chunks, partition them by compiler action-mode identity, and retain one scored roster entry for every supported mode rather than only the largest cluster. The input is the edited scene, task specification, and compiler-generated feasible solutions; the output is an alternative-positive roster A+ with mode identities and roster-size metadata.
plain_method_steps_en.why_this_makes_sense: A mode-indexed roster makes positive coverage and worst-mode retention visible and prevents dominant-mode aggregation from hiding feasible alternatives.

plain_method_steps_en.what_to_do: Under the edited observation, evaluate trainable and frozen-reference action scores for the invalid chunk and each feasible alternative, form their reference-adjusted difference, and apply a soft feasible-over-invalid preference only at times selected by m. The input is the violation mask, invalid chunk, alternative-positive roster, edited observation, and frozen reference policy; the output is boundary preference loss L_B and per-mode margins d_theta.
plain_method_steps_en.why_this_makes_sense: Reference adjustment isolates post-training movement, while the mask directs feasibility credit to the counterfactual’s implicated segment rather than the whole chunk.

plain_method_steps_en.what_to_do: Penalize reference-adjusted score drift outside m for all rostered chunks and add an equal-per-mode score anchor for every feasible alternative, without pooling alternatives by frequency. The input is reference-adjusted scores, the mask complement, and the full alternative-positive roster; the output is complement loss L_comp and alternative-preservation loss L_alt.
plain_method_steps_en.why_this_makes_sense: The complement term prevents temporal credit leakage, and the alternative term makes suppressing minority feasible modes costly even when average validity improves.

plain_method_steps_en.what_to_do: Add L_B, L_comp, and L_alt to ordinary imitation. Select their symbolic weights on validation pairs by first preventing complement and worst-mode degradation and then improving boundary separation; freeze the selected weights. Report M_B with eligibility, mask-length, roster-size, drift, coverage, and worst-mode summaries. The input is imitation batches and the three BLSM loss terms; the output is a post-trained continuous-action VLA and boundary-mechanism diagnostics.
plain_method_steps_en.why_this_makes_sense: The selection rule prevents an arbitrary loss-weight trade-off from standing in for the mechanism, while the diagnostics connect score movement to reliability and retention.

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 对原始 RoboTwin 2.0 场景中由冻结策略成功执行的每个动作片段，搜索保持任务不变的几何编辑，并保留使同一片段失败的最低成本编辑。记录每个尝试过的成对样本及纳入或排除原因。输入是原始场景、任务指令、冻结策略动作片段和模拟器可行性检查；输出是接受的原始/编辑 BoundaryFlip 对及完整的资格记录。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 固定任务和动作身份后，几何变化就是预期差异，也能显示合格边界对是否超出数据中的某个被挑选角落。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 在两个场景中重放同一动作片段，计算每个动作时刻的模拟器违规指示，并将 m 设为编辑场景中的第一个连续违规区间，而不是标记整个片段。输入是接受的 BoundaryFlip 对和同步模拟器轨迹；输出是非空的首次违规掩码 m 及其补集。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 该掩码来自观测到的模拟器结构，确定几何编辑首次改变功能有效性的时间区域。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 在编辑场景中运行任务编译器，枚举可行动作片段，按编译器的动作模式身份划分，并为每个受支持模式保留一个有得分的名册条目，而不只保留最大簇。输入是编辑场景、任务规格和编译器生成的可行解；输出是带模式身份和名册大小元数据的替代正例名册 A+。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 按模式编制名册使正例覆盖率和最差模式保留率可见，并防止主导模式聚合隐藏可行替代方案。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 在编辑后观测下，计算无效片段及每个可行替代方案的可训练策略和冻结参考策略动作得分，形成参考调整后的差值，并只在 m 选出的时刻施加可行优于无效的软偏好。输入是违规掩码、无效动作片段、替代正例名册、编辑后观测和冻结参考策略；输出是边界偏好损失 L_B 及逐模式间隔 d_theta。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 参考调整隔离训练后的移动，而掩码将可行性得分归因指向反事实涉及的片段，而非整个动作片段。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 对所有名册片段在 m 之外的参考调整得分漂移进行惩罚，并为每个可行替代方案加入等模式权重的得分锚定，不按频率合并替代方案。输入是参考调整后的得分、掩码补集和完整替代正例名册；输出是补集损失 L_comp 和替代保留损失 L_alt。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 补集项防止时间信用泄漏，替代项使压制少数可行模式变得有代价，即使平均有效性提高。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 将 L_B、L_comp 和 L_alt 加入普通模仿目标。在验证对上先防止补集和最差模式退化，再改善边界分离，以此选择符号权重并冻结选定权重。报告 M_B，以及资格、掩码长度、名册大小、漂移、覆盖率和最差模式摘要。输入是模仿批次和三个 BLSM 损失项；输出是训练后的连续动作 VLA 和边界机制诊断。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 该选择规则避免任意损失权衡冒充机制，而公开的诊断把得分移动与下游可靠性和保留率联系起来。

plain_method_modules_en.purpose_oneline: Construct accepted geometry-flip pairs, certify their first violation segment, and enumerate supported feasible modes.
Apply boundary-local preference while anchoring the complement and every feasible alternative.
Select frozen loss weights and expose boundary, validity, drift, coverage, and worst-mode diagnostics.

plain_method_modules_zh.purpose_oneline: 构造可接受的几何翻转对，认证其首次违规区间，并枚举受支持的可行模式。
施加边界局部偏好，同时锚定补集和每个可行替代方案。
选择冻结的损失权重，并公开边界、有效性、漂移、覆盖率和最差模式诊断。

falsification_prediction: Post-train the same continuous-action π0.5 initialization on BoundaryFlip-RoboTwin pairs and compare ordinary imitation, global feasibility supervision, whole-chunk preference tuning, and the proposed objective on held-out task and geometry families. If the mechanism works, edited-scene success rises and invalid-mode execution falls relative to ordinary imitation, while alternative-positive coverage and worst-mode success remain higher and complement score drift remains lower than under global and whole-chunk shaping. The load-bearing variable is the mean held-out boundary margin M_B = E[d_θ]; permuting violation masks or positive/invalid pair identities while holding data volume and all loss weights fixed should collapse the edited-scene success and mode-coverage advantage, not merely change M_B. If those permutations preserve the downstream advantage, or if L_alt removal leaves worst-mode success unchanged while coverage is already high, boundary-local credit and alternative-positive preservation are not the operative causes. As mandatory pre-training gates, report eligibility among all compiler-attempted pairs, the complete mask-length and roster-size distributions, and each excluded pair's exclusion reason plus frozen-policy edited-scene success and invalid-mode execution; no downstream mechanism claim is eligible unless these gates show that proper boundary runs and alternative-mode rosters occur beyond a negligible selected subset.
compute_budget: Approximately 56 A100-80GB GPU-days for simulator-conditioned post-training, four baselines, mask/preservation ablations, and repeated held-out evaluations; on the available 4xA100 allocation this is about 14 wall-days and is comfortable within one paper cycle. No paid APIs are used; simulator pair generation is a modest scripted RoboTwin 2.0 resource and runs separately on CPU workers.
what_step_was_missed: It would have needed to pair the identical successful action across a minimum feasibility-flipping geometry edit, extract the first causal violation mask, and use that mask in a reference-adjusted score preference while independently anchoring every feasible alternative mode; its available abstract establishes only a simple geometry-grounded feasibility objective.

compute.rationale: GPU line ≈ 56 vs 4 GPU-day (1400%) → infeasible. Overall (worse line) → infeasible.

data.rationale: RoboTwin 2.0 scenes, scripted geometry edits, simulator traces, and continuous-action policy rollouts are nameable accessible sources, and the required positive rosters can be generated by the same task compiler.

theoretical.rationale: No theorem is load-bearing; the equations define an empirical score-shaping objective and identifiable diagnostics rather than a formal theoretical contribution.

engineering.rationale: The binding implementation cost is robust minimum-edit search plus synchronized first-violation and mode-roster extraction across many simulator pairs, although each component is scriptable with existing RoboTwin tooling.

falsification.rationale: The held-out boundary margin, mask and identity permutations, alternative-anchor removal, and downstream validity and retention metrics are concrete interventions measurable with the same simulator and score interface.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Where the abstract reports a simple geometry-grounded feasibility objective, this candidate constructs same-action minimal geometry flips, assigns preference credit only to the first simulator-certified violation segment, and separately protects every compiler-enumerated positive mode (abstract-only inference because full text was unavailable).

Where STARRY jointly denoises future spatial-temporal latents and actions with depth-conditioned attention, this candidate measures a reference-adjusted local score margin from counterfactual validity flips and constrains score drift outside the causal segment (abstract-only inference because full text was unavailable).

Where Action Manifold Learning predicts on a geometry-guided valid manifold, this candidate explicitly audits and optimizes worst-mode retention when one previously valid action becomes invalid under a minimal geometry edit (abstract-only inference because full text was unavailable).

Where KeyStone executes the medoid of the largest sampled action cluster, this candidate post-trains a boundary-local conditional score while treating minority feasible modes as protected positives rather than candidates to discard (abstract-only inference because full text was unavailable).

Where GEAR-VLA integrates aligned 3D features and a canonicalized continuous-action expert, this candidate constructs a temporal counterfactual credit signal and a matched mode-retention diagnostic without adding an oracle geometry channel at inference (abstract-only inference because full text was unavailable).

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Paper-pointed threat: Can Explicit Physical Feasibility Benefit VLA Learning? (lit_table). From the available abstract, this work can subsume the broad claim that explicit geometry feasibility should suppress invalid robot actions. The present candidate is only distinguishable by first-violation localization, complement retention, and compiler-relative worst-mode preservation; the available record is insufficient to verify that those mechanisms are absent from the full paper.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses.response: The defense is anchored in method steps S1-S5 and the locked falsification prediction: the claimed delta is the conjunction of same-action minimum edits, first-violation localization, complement anchoring, and compiler-relative worst-mode preservation, not the broad use of feasibility supervision. Because the threatening paper is available only at abstract level, this remains a conditional distinction; full-text verification must show that it does not already implement that conjunction.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Un-retrieved mechanism family flagged by the audit (parametric knowledge, not in the retrieved pool): Novelty coverage is materially degraded: arXiv collision retrieval returned 0, only 2 of 25 literature records have full text, and 6 host references remain unresolved. The many lexical collision hits do not contain an identified exact mechanism, but they cannot compensate for the missing primary evidence; a nearby feasibility-weighting or local-credit family remains unexcluded. — novelty vs this family is UNVERIFIED; run a targeted scoop-check on that vocabulary before investing.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses.response: A targeted scoop-check must establish that the feasibility-weighting or local-credit family does not already combine minimum same-action geometry flips, reference-adjusted first-violation preference, complement-drift control, and mode-wise positive preservation. Finding that joint mechanism would remove the candidate's novelty delta even if its terminology differs.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Gap-closure reject-check borderline on gap 1 (C04): Presenting a sensitivity or redundancy proxy as the novelty invites the verdict that it rediscovers known mixed-precision or low-rank results unless it is sharply differentiated from the obvious prior; Skipping any analysis of why the heterogeneity exists - the data or value distribution that drives the partition - makes the technical novelty and the potential impact impossible to assess.; Bolting together established components (distillation plus pruning plus calibration) without an error bound or artifact specific to the new setting reads as incremental even when the target applicatio
reviewer_concerns_and_responses.response: The decomposition in S2 is not a sensitivity or redundancy proxy: it is the first simulator-certified violation run induced by the minimum functional-geometry edit, and S4-S5 assign the distinct treatments uniquely implied by boundary membership. The heterogeneity is therefore explained by where execution validity first changes, while the complement and per-mode anchors make the proposal more than a bundle of generic compression or calibration components.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Gap-closure reject-check borderline on gap 2 (C02): A diagnostic that only re-confirms a shortcut already known in advance, surfacing no previously unmeasurable failure, is read as confirmatory rather than as a contribution.; Validating a synthetic-ground-truth instrument only on synthetic data, without demonstrating that the controlled finding transfers to real-world instances, leaves ecological validity unestablished and; Building the instrument around one contested definition of the target property means it cannot independently confirm that the definition is correct, and reviewers flag the resulting circularity.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses.response: The diagnostic does more than reconfirm that geometry matters: it measures the previously conflated sign split between invalid-action suppression and retention of each still-feasible action mode. The eligibility ledger, held-out task and geometry families, frozen-policy outcomes for exclusions, and mask or pair-identity permutations reduce selection and definitional circularity; transfer beyond RoboTwin remains an open ecological-validity limit rather than a claimed result.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Anti-pattern matched: audit_decomp_supervisor. Required mitigation: The decomposition criterion must be derivable from observed structure or task-level supervision (not just intuition), AND the manufactured signal must be the unique signal the decomposition implies. An ablation that holds the decomposition fixed and varies the signal (or vice versa) must show the two are not conflated.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses.response: S2 derives the decomposition from the observed first simulator-certified violation run under a task-preserving geometry flip, and S4 manufactures exactly the corresponding masked preference while S5 anchors the implied complement. The locked falsification prediction separates decomposition from signal by permuting masks or pair identities and tests the independent preservation mechanism through L_alt removal, so a gain that survives those interventions does not support the proposed explanation.

domain_landscape.position_note: BLSM combines a saturated heterogeneous-decomposition pattern (9 of 18 papers) with the scarcely used controlled-diagnostic pattern (1 of 18), using the former for boundary-local treatment and the latter to expose its reliability-versus-mode-retention consequence.
